name: The operation that selects which of several possible ordered forms a pool of units settles into by introducing one already-ordered unit as a template whose handedness and arrangement the growing lattice copies; a choice of one form among the several a mixture could otherwise adopt, distinct from the untemplated growth that takes whichever ordered form is lowest by default.

phase_0.domain_name: The operation that selects which of several possible ordered forms a pool of units settles into by introducing one already-ordered unit as a template whose handedness and arrangement the growing lattice copies; a choice of one form among the several a mixture could otherwise adopt, distinct from the untemplated growth that takes whichever ordered form is lowest by default.
phase_0.boundary_condition: The Gibbs free energy landscape defining possible crystal polymorphs.

VINIT.justification: The unorganized state where no specific lattice structure exists yet.

TANCH.justification: The final macroscopic boundary that contains all unit cells in the selected phase.

AFWD.justification: The forward addition of units to the growing interface.

AREV.justification: The removal of a unit from the lattice back into the pool.

CLINK.justification: The sequential binding of individual monomers into a chain or layer.

IMSCRIB.justification: The matching of a new unit to the existing local symmetry of the lattice.

FSPLIT.justification: The fork between autonomous stochastic nucleation and template-directed growth.

FFUSE.justification: The convergence of either growth path into a stable crystalline state.

EVALT.justification: Successful adoption of the template chiral handedness.

EVALF.justification: Growth into a default or stochastic form lacking template influence.

ENGAGR.justification: A state where multiple contradictory chiral domains coexist in one crystal.

IFIX.justification: The permanent locking of a unit into the crystal interior, protected from the pool.

phase_3.void_description: Disordered monomer pool with no long-range correlation.
phase_3.true_description: Highly ordered lattice following the specific template symmetry.
phase_3.false_description: Low-energy default lattice or random polymorph configuration.
phase_3.both_description: Metastable coexistence of templated and default configurations.

steps.domain_action: Establish the disordered pool of chemical units.
Determine if a template unit is introduced to the system.
Identify the presence of a chiral template.
Initiate growth along the template coordinate.
Verify the local unit matches the template symmetry.
Permanently record the first templated layer.
Append subsequent units to the templated seed.
Reject units that do not match the template orientation.
Consolidate templated units into a unified lattice grain.
Fork the process for untemplated stochastic growth.
Acknowledge the absence or failure of template influence.
Allow units to settle into the lowest default energy state.
Enforce consistency with the locally dominant stochastic seed.
Permanently record the default lattice orientation.
Build outward through untemplated thermal addition.
Recombine mass into the default bulk crystal.
Close the system boundary around the final ordered mass.

phase_5.compiler_frontend: Chemical kinetics determining the rate of addition vs subtraction.
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: Surface-to-monomer collision and hydrogen bonding signals.
phase_5.memory_mechanism: The existing lattice surface acting as a physical record of prior choices.
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: Diffusion-limited transport of units from the pool to the growth site.
phase_5.alfs_store: Thermodynamic data tables for the specific polymorph configurations.

phase_6.cycle_cost: Release of the latent heat of crystallization.
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: High-entropy liquid or gaseous monomer distribution.
phase_6.post_cycle_state: Low-entropy ordered solid lattice and dissipated heat.
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — The reduction in configuration entropy is compensated by heat release to the environment.
